title: Evolution and implementation of EU regulation on new genomic techniques
key_claim: Regulation (EU) 2026/1388 on plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques and their products was adopted by the European Union on 17 June 2026, twenty-five years after Directive 2001/18/EC and nineteen years after the Commission's first Working Group on New Plant Breeding Techniques was established in 2007.
frame_summary: Cardi and Vitale frame the Regulation as the long-delayed alignment of EU law with the science, dating the achievement against a quarter-century of legislative stasis rather than against the access and ownership questions the Regulation leaves open.
verbatim_quote: With the approval of the European Council and the European Parliament, Regulation (EU) 2026/1388 on plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques and their products was finally adopted by the European Union on 17 June 2026.

title: Plant Gene-Editing Regulation Roundup (July 2026)
date_evidence: Client Alert # Plant Gene-Editing Regulation Roundup 17 Jul 2026
key_claim: The EU rules shift regulation from the technique used to create a plant toward its final characteristics. Category 1 NGT plants may have substitutions or insertions of fewer than 20 nucleotides, deletions, or other changes achievable by traditional breeding, and are exempted from GMO regulation; Category 2 plants remain GMOs. The regulation entered into force on 16 July 2026 and will be fully applied by 17 July 2028. Argentina's Resolucion 255/2026, published in March 2026, streamlined its gene-editing approvals into a single three-step procedure, and Pakistan approved its National Agriculture Biotechnology Policy in June 2026, exempting SDN-1 and SDN-2 plants from GMO rules.
frame_summary: Morrison Foerster frames 2026 as a year of converging streamlining across three jurisdictions, advising clients that the regulatory route to market is shortening and saying nothing about intellectual property as a constraint on that route.
verbatim_quote: Category 1 NGT plants can have small targeted genetic changes (substitutions or insertions of less than 20 nucleotides), deletions, or other changes that could have been made through traditional breeding.
verbatim_list: The new rules represent a shift away from regulating plants according to the techniques used to create them and toward regulation based on their final characteristics.
The new regulations entered into force July 16, 2026 and will be fully applied by July 17, 2028.
Category 1 plants will now be treated like conventionally bred plants and will be exempted from GMO regulations.
Pakistan approved the National Agriculture Biotechnology Policy of Pakistan 2025 in June 2026.

title: EU Approves New Genomic Techniques (NGT) Rules: What Gene-Edited Plant Developers Need to Know
date_evidence: ## EU Approves New Genomic Techniques (NGT) Rules: What Gene-Edited Plant Developers Need to Know June 17, 2026
key_claim: The Council formally adopted the NGT regulation on 21 April 2026 and the European Parliament gave final approval on 17 June 2026. NGT plants remain patentable except for traits or sequences occurring in nature or produced by biological means. The regulation relies on transparency rather than the complete patent ban Parliament had once pushed for: developers must declare patents in a public database, and the Commission plans a code of conduct and an expert group. Even NGT-1 plants must be registered in a public EU database and all seed and reproductive material must be labelled as NGT-1, so these materials will not in practice be treated the same as conventional products. Herbicide-tolerant plants and those producing insecticidal substances cannot qualify as NGT-1.
frame_summary: Written by a patent attorney for plant-developer clients, this piece frames the reform as positive for innovators but corrects the headline reading, arguing that the practical constraints have moved to registration, labelling, national fragmentation and, above all, licensing complexity.

title: Neue Gentechnik (NGT): Kommt das Saatgut-Patent-Verbot? Was Landwirtschaftsminister jetzt fordern (German)
key_claim: The German federal-state agriculture ministers' conference (Agrarministerkonferenz) resolved by majority in late March 2026 to seek an amendment to the EU Biotech Directive 98/44/EC introducing a full breeders' exemption equivalent to the one in German plant variety protection law, so that breeders could work with patented NGT seed without the patent holder's permission or royalties. Despite the existing prohibition on patenting essentially biological processes, the European Patent Office granted around 40 patents on conventionally bred plants in 2025. IG Saatgut warns that NGT patents can also cover coincidentally identical conventionally bred plants, impairing conventional breeding even before deregulation applies; Testbiotech warns of further market concentration. The December 2025 trilogue settled on transparency obligations and a voluntary code of conduct rather than a patent restriction.
frame_summary: A German patent-attorney firm arguing that a full seed-patent ban is unlikely in the short term and that the realistic corrective is a full breeders' exemption written into the Biotech Directive, with freedom-to-operate risk remaining the operative issue for seed companies and farms until then.

title: EU approves New Genomic Techniques for plants
date_evidence: # EU approves New Genomic Techniques for plants 08 July 2026 Science and Innovation ... By Jenny Brunton, Senior European Policy Advisor
key_claim: On 17 June 2026 the European Parliament approved the NGT legislation; the text was published in the Official Journal on 26 June 2026 and entered into force on 16 July 2026, with a two-year implementation period. Patent rules remain governed by the EU Biotech Directive; applicants to register a category 1 NGT plant must submit information on all existing or pending patents into a publicly available database, and may voluntarily provide information on the patent holder's intention to licence under equitable conditions. Council and Parliament agreed to create a patenting expert group composed of experts from all member states, the European Patent Office and the Community Plant Variety Office. One year after entry into force the Commission will publish a study on the impact of patenting on innovation, on the availability of seeds to farmers and on the competitiveness of the EU plant breeding sector, then indicate follow-up measures or publish a legislative proposal. Northern Ireland continues to follow EU plant rules under the EU-UK TCA.

title: NGT update: European Parliament adopts deregulation rules and rejects seed patent amendments
date_evidence: # NGT update: European Parliament adopts deregulation rules and rejects seed patent amendments 18 Jun 2026 | By William Nichols
key_claim: On 17 June 2026 the European Parliament adopted the NGT regulation by 431 votes to 201 with 29 abstentions, and rejected amendments that would have curbed patents on seeds. IFOAM Organics Europe secured two safeguards, the continued prohibition of NGTs in organic production and labelling of seed lots containing NGTs, but says patents remain the most worrying unresolved issue. Arche Noah's Paul Grabenberger says the adopted text honours neither of Parliament's 2024 demands for NGT labelling and a seed patent ban, and that Arche Noah's analysis counts roughly 2,000 NGT patent applications worldwide covering seeds, plants and silage. Euroseeds issued a statement of support signed by 30 European agri-food organisations including Copa-Cogeca, EuropaBio, FoodDrinkEurope and CropLife Europe.
frame_summary: Food Ingredients First frames the vote as a contested settlement in which the organic and civil-society side lost the patent argument while the agri-food value chain gained legal clarity, and reports both camps' positions without adjudicating between them.
verbatim_quote: The vote passed with 431 Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) voting to adopt the regulation, with 201 MEPs voting against, and 29 abstentions.
verbatim_list: the European Parliament adopted contested rules deregulating plants made with new genomic techniques (NGTs), and rejected amendments that would have curbed patents on seeds
Grabenberger also notes that, according to Arche Noah’s analysis, there are roughly 2,000 NGT patent applications worldwide, including patents that cover seeds, plants, and silage.
Yet, the group says patents remain the most worrying unresolved issue.

title: Agricultural Crop Licensing Platform: background on patented traits and breeders' access
date_evidence: meta-article:modified_time: 2026-08-31T12:33:47+00:00 (page last modified; no publication date is stated for the background text)
key_claim: The ACLP is Europe's licensing platform for patented traits in agricultural, ornamental, fruit and forest crops. Its background material states that plant breeding is estimated to be responsible for more than 60% of annual productivity growth; that breeders can use each other's commercial varieties through the breeders' exemption in the plant variety rights system, but that patent laws in most European countries provide no statutory limited breeders' exemption for a patented trait contained in a commercial variety and require further licence obligations; and that the act of breeding with a patented plant could be seen as patent infringement even where the breeder has no interest in the patented trait. Patent-holding members must disclose all patents in their commercial varieties and grant a licence to any member requesting access, under a standard agreement with arbitration.
frame_summary: An industry-run licensing platform arguing that the access problem created by plant patents is real but soluble by voluntary, standardised private licensing rather than by changing patent law.
verbatim_quote: However, if a patented trait is contained in a commercial variety, patent laws in most European countries do not provide for a statutory limited breeder’s exemption and require further license obligations between plant breeders and patent holders.
